newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea 3-yr yields end higher on drying liquidity.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea 3-yr yields end higher on drying liquidity.

text.p: Yields on three-year corporates closed higher on Friday as liquidity dried up after the central bank's announcement of money absorption through repurchase agreements, brokers said.
The three-month CDs remained unchanged with few new issues, and the overnight call rate edged up due to rising money demand for salary and tax payments, they said.
* 3-yr corporates end at 12.40 pct from 12.38 on Thursday
Yields on three-year corporate bonds ended higher on Friday as liquidity tightened after the central bank's announcement of money absorption through repurchase agreements, brokers said.
"The Bank of Korea's repo operation seemed to signal that the bank will tighten money supply to fight inflation," said Kim Yun, a broker at Daewoo Securities.
The central bank said in early afternoon it would siphon off 500 billion won through three-day repos. It later said actual absorbed amount totalled 350 billion won.
The three-month CDs remained flat with few new issues.
The overnight call rate edged up due to rising money demand in the short-term money market.
Money demand tends to rise towards the end of the month because of salary and tax payments.
New issues of the three-year corporates were estimated at 160 billion won today, compared with 235 billion on Thursday.
